claims.statement: For R=aH^2+2HL+T with H cap-one and independent of the later bank, L density cap M, arbitrary correlated T, and arbitrary real a, |phi_R(t)|<=min(1,sqrt(pi M/|t|)).
For every 0<gamma<1/2, H_gamma(R)<=C_gamma M^gamma uniformly in a; at gamma=1/4 the constant is 3.179662567631707.

Two source-disjoint literal scalar squares plus the random-modulation residual give ||p_Q||_infinity<=11.745890746379832 |b0|^-1/2 |b1|^-1/3 M^1/6; for original-coordinate linear modulation row norm c, <=12.444337756165789 |b0|^-1/2 |b1|^-1/3 c^-1/6.
Under random modulation alone, gamma=1/2 is false: iid H,Y uniform[-1/2,1/2], a=1, L=Y, T=Y^2 gives R=(H+Y)^2 and E|R|^-1/2=infinity. This is rank one and not a QFORM counterexample.

partner_result_applied.application: For Q_(epsilon,m)=X0^2+Z^2+epsilon H^2+2H m^-1/2 sum_jY_j, after peeling X0^2 the residual has literal Z pivot one and s2>=1, so ||p_Q||_infinity<=8+32sqrt(5)4^-1/8=68.1696494893823 uniformly in m and epsilon.

strict_target_application.spectral_reason: two literal eigenvalues one plus the star 2x2 eigenvalues have product -1, so at least one star eigenvalue has modulus at least one
strict_target_application.new_bound: ||p_Q||_infinity<12.445 uniformly in m, epsilon, and all admissible product laws

next_step: In the one-outer-pivot diffuse-row survivor with s2>=1, use the inherited second spectral direction to upgrade the curvature-uniform H_gamma, gamma<1/2, to H_1/2 without demanding a second literal square and without conditioning away product provenance.
